keyword: what is a super el nino
claims: A "super" El Niño is an informal term for an exceptionally strong El Niño event.
Pacific sea surface temperatures rise at least 2°C (3.6°F) above normal in a super El Niño.
Super El Niños occur roughly every 10 to 20 years.
A super El Niño is characterized by Oceanic Nino Index (ONI) 3.4 values of +2.0°C or greater, sustained over several months.
Notable past super El Niño events include 1982–83, 1997–98, and 2015–16.
Super El Niños typically lead to wetter, cooler conditions in the southern U.S.
Super El Niños typically lead to warmer, drier conditions in the northern U.S.
Super El Niños generally increase tropical activity in the Pacific.
Super El Niños suppress tropical activity in the Atlantic due to increased wind shear.
